title: Cost of the junta restriction program
statement: Let $n,k,M\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $P\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and fix an assignment $z$ on $P$. Let $\delta$ satisfy $0<\delta\le\tfrac12$. Every outcome in the support of the program's run with target $f$ has cost $(S,0,S+W)$, where $S$ is the program's defined sample count and $W$ its defined sample work for $P,k,M,\delta$.
hypotheses_covered: Outcome belongs to the support of the program run
